fitReason: Visitor-first, lower-physical-confidence backup for CS work on neural decoding, signal processing or model-based assistive control. The current joining page explicitly values AI/reinforcement-learning and software experience. This is a specialized neural-engineering route rather than a general-purpose robot-learning lab, and a suitable short computational project must be agreed with the PI.

physicalEvidence.summary: The lab’s full 2025 NER paper describes trained velocity-Kalman decoding of neural spikes and linear-regression EMG decoding driving a real seven-degree-of-freedom Tecnalia exoskeleton. However, it explicitly reports a single participant’s 2017–2021 ISMORE trial in Spain. This is genuine older collaborative physical execution, not evidence of a current Berkeley exoskeleton, a fresh 2025 robot trial or visitor hardware access. Current local research emphasizes sensorimotor network modeling, closed-loop brain-machine tasks and movement sensing. Contemporary local robot deployment remains unverified, so this record belongs in the lower-physical-confidence research-backup tier.

shortVisit.summary: The live Sensorimotor Neural Engineering Lab joining page explicitly recruits master’s students and visiting students, asks applicants to contact Khanna with their CV and research interests, and highlights AI/reinforcement learning, software engineering and signal-processing experience. It does not specify eight weeks, summer 2027, stipend, self-funding terms or remote participation. Its separate Spring 2026 Berkeley-undergraduate job and Fall 2027 degree-admission subject line are not an external summer visit offer.
